A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaMa and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B. Matching retained content across renumbering and relocation supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BAD-ACTS experiments, attack-transfer evaluations, model-selection results, and an initial-archive ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds AgentDojo evaluations, further model-transfer results, and safety–quality sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The structured system representation, adversarial search, archive sampling, and design loop in Sections 3–4 and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The additional experiments vary existing controls and weighted archive selection without establishing a changed MaMa algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on AgentDojo's Workspace and Slack environments in Figure 2, extending coverage beyond the four retained BAD-ACTS environments. Section 5.1 explicitly excludes AgentDojo travel planning because of overlap with existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the quality-only variant, Guardian Agents, LPTG plus Tool Filtering, and the Delimiters defense. The added AgentDojo panels use the existing comparator set. GLM and Nemotron are additional agent-model configurations; the newly cited Guardian method is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Added experiments use GLM-4.7-flash and Nemotron-3-Super agents, design-time compromise budgets of two and three agents, and varying post-training selection weights. Existing metrics and principal budgets remain unchanged. The 25-attack budget newly emphasized in Section 5.1 was already documented in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends safety–quality analysis by testing optimization against multiple compromised agents (Table 3) and post-training archive-selection weights (Appendix A.3, Figure 5). Table 2 also broadens model-transfer testing. The original test-time adversary-count study and empty-archive ablation are retained.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their three-evaluation and standard-deviation reporting, and the added Table 2 rows follow the existing mean-and-standard-deviation convention. No additional seed information, revised run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds Workspace and Slack trajectories, additional model-transfer scores, and results for adversary-count and selection-weight sweeps. For example, Table 2 adds Code Generation safety of 4.93 (0.09) for GLM-4.7-flash against Qwen3:32b. Existing table entries remain unchanged apart from equivalent formatting; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The system definition, attack-distance constraint, best-response formulation, leader objective, and archive-sampling mathematics are retained. Appendix A.3 reexpresses the existing weighted quality–safety aggregation for selection analysis; it adds no substantive formal property, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim that MaMa approximately solves the game with the narrower description that it is inspired by the formalization. The conclusion also limits the safety comparison to the evaluated attack scenario. The central automated-design and robustness contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific limitation about benchmarks not capturing real agentic systems and discusses resource-constrained optimization. It also interprets optimization against more adversaries as trading quality for safety. That interpretation is overgeneralized: Table 3 reports Code Generation safety falling from 4.6 to 4.0.

D1.justification: v2 provides an explicit code-repository link in the abstract and removes v1's generic statement that final-system code accompanies the supplementary material. Hardware, runtimes, API cost, hyperparameters, and appendix prompts are otherwise retained. The PDFs establish changed access information, not verification of the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Related work adds multi-agent code-execution attacks, graph-based defenses, communication-structure research, and further game-theoretic references, including Triedman, Zhou, Huang, Brückner and Scheffer, Mohammadi, and Rajeswaran. These broaden context without replacing the central positioning around AFlow and automated safe-system design. Other reference edits largely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the abstract, introduction, methodological explanations, and conclusion, plus a new appendix subsection and acknowledgments. Publication and affiliation text also change. The main section order, most prose, and virtually all appendix prompt text are retained.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands substantially: Figure 2 becomes a six-panel display, Table 2 gains model rows, and Table 3 and the four-panel Figure 5 are added. Existing appendix plots are restyled; the empty-archive figure uses compact step plots and a shared legend in v2 Figure 7. Retained displays also move and are renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the AgentDojo and additional model-transfer evaluations provide useful evidence beyond the original benchmark, while narrower claims and explicit code-access information improve clarity. The gains are limited by problems in the new analyses: Table 3 overstates safety benefits, and Figure 5 shows quality decreasing as the stated formula gives quality greater weight. These weaknesses temper the benefit of the broader evaluation.
